how_these_were_chosen: The run date as a plain integer, and its successor for the reserve. Chosen because the rule they serve is that the number must be fixed BEFORE a result is seen, not that it be unpredictable — a date is checkable against this file's own git timestamp, which is the property that matters. No seed here was drawn from a prior run, from the served template (whose sampler carried 923510416338945 under control_after_generate=randomize), or from anything this seat had already looked at.

ceiling.why_machine_readable: specs/ceiling-why-machine-readable.md - ONE home for this block's correction history and its seven citations into tools/. Moved there in swarm wave 28 (F-7ca576d2): eight byte-identical copies of one 4,984-character paragraph were 49.9% of every byte under specs/, sitting between an operator and the bound on the one resource in this repo with no compensator. Nothing was deleted - the correction history is more useful than the original and is kept verbatim at that path, with each RE-ANCHORED note appended in place. The values that BIND this spend are beside this line: submissions, counted_in, note, and the per-arm or per-wave split where the experiment has one.

binds_in_both_directions: An experiment that pre-registered seeds must use one of them, and an experiment that pre-registered none may not vary its seed at all. tools/armature_core/route_gates.py::gate_s_registration enforces both clauses in code against the graph that is about to run, and ignores the inert seed of an add_noise=disable sampler because demanding registration there would be a check that fires on a correct two-expert split.
